stories.title: Burnham Unveils £442m Rough Sleeping Plan
stories.summary: PM Andy Burnham announces a £442m package providing emergency accommodation and health support to end rough sleeping in England.

stories.title: Burnham Set to Disappoint Labour MPs on Donation Caps
stories.summary: Downing Street signals it will not pursue a cap on political donations despite pressure from Labour MPs concerned about Reform UK's big-money backers.

stories.title: Poll: British Voters Mixed on Burnham's First Week
stories.summary: A POLITICO poll shows Burnham generating interest but a majority of voters want him to call an early election rather than continuing the inherited mandate.

stories.title: 🏗️ Police Floats £90m Contract for New Public Digital Channels
stories.summary: A new £90m contract to support public-facing digital channels across policing has emerged — a significant procurement signal in the public safety tech space.

stories.title: 🤖 Government Uses Image Recognition AI to Tackle EV Grant Fraud
stories.summary: Government agencies are deploying AI image recognition tools to detect fraud in EV grant applications, signalling broader AI adoption in public sector enforcement.

stories.title: 🏗️ HMRC Seeks £4.5m Partner to Replace Legacy Metadata System with AI Platform
stories.summary: HMRC is sourcing a supplier to replace a legacy metadata system with an AI-powered platform — a key digital transformation and procurement signal.

stories.title: 🏢 MoD Signs £16m Microsoft Deal for Cyber and Espionage Defence
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence has contracted Microsoft for £16m to detect and disrupt cyber and espionage threats — a notable vendor signal for US tech in UK defence.

stories.title: 🏗️ HMRC Selects Atos, Coforge and Cognizant as Low Code Partners (DALAS Framework)
stories.summary: HMRC has selected three suppliers under the DALAS framework for low-code platform delivery — a significant procurement decision for government digital services.

stories.title: 🤖 Government Chief Data Officer: Time to Get Public Sector Data Working Together
stories.summary: The Government Chief Data Officer highlights the urgent need for NHS and public sector data interoperability, flagging that siloed systems are failing citizens.

stories.title: 🚦 What Has Burnham Promised Since Becoming PM — and When Will It Happen?
stories.summary: The Guardian tracks Burnham's growing list of pledges — from housing costs to public ownership of utilities — raising delivery timeline questions with ~3 years left in Parliament.

stories.title: Parliament in Summer Recess — Recorded Proceedings on BBC
stories.summary: Parliament is in summer recess with BBC Parliament airing recorded sessions. No new live debates or legislation until Parliament returns in September.

stories.title: Labour 'Could Lose Up to 50 Seats' to Greens Over North Sea Drilling
stories.summary: Environmental groups warn that permitting any new North Sea drilling could cost Labour up to 50 seats to the Green Party at the next general election.

stories.title: Labour Demands Tice Apologise to Firefighters Over 'Enjoy It' Heat Remark
stories.summary: Labour has called on Reform UK's Richard Tice to apologise after he appeared to tell firefighters to 'enjoy' the extreme heatwave, calling the remark irresponsible.

stories.title: Starmer Allies See 'Hint of Retribution' in Burnham Reshuffle
stories.summary: Former PM Keir Starmer's allies have voiced concern that Andy Burnham's cabinet reshuffle contained elements of political payback against Starmer loyalists.

stories.title: Badenoch Attacks Burnham's Economic Plans — PM Responds with Comebacks
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch challenged PM Burnham over his economic programme, though Burnham reportedly had strong prepared responses to her attacks.

stories.title: Davey Calls for UK to Join EU Migration and Asylum Framework
stories.summary: Lib Dem leader Ed Davey has called on Burnham to tackle small boat crossings by joining the EU's new migration and asylum framework, and wants a Commons vote on the matter.

stories.title: Westminster Constituency Becomes Lib Dem Target Seat
stories.summary: Politico reports that Westminster constituency has been identified as a new Lib Dem target seat — a notable development in the heart of British politics.

stories.summary: The Guardian's analysis concludes that Nigel Farage's decision to trigger the Clacton by-election was a miscalculation, bringing him 'full circle' without meaningful political gain.

stories.title: Reform UK Ridiculed: 'They Deserve a Slot on the Edinburgh Fringe'
stories.summary: A Guardian opinion piece argues Reform politicians have become a political joke, with their controversies increasingly compared to comedy festival material.

stories.title: Richard Tice Under Fire for 'Enjoy It' Remark to Firefighters During Heatwave
stories.summary: Reform UK's Richard Tice faces calls to apologise after remarks appearing to dismiss the danger of extreme heat conditions to fire and emergency service personnel.

stories.title: Analysis: The Dangers of Politicians Being 'Too Online' — or Not Online Enough
stories.summary: A BBC piece examines how Scottish and UK parties (including the SNP) navigate social media strategy, and whether being too online or too offline can damage political credibility.

stories.title: Scottish Greens Back UNESCO Bid for Morning Roll Recognition
stories.summary: The Scottish Greens have thrown their weight behind a campaign to secure UNESCO recognition for Scotland's beloved morning roll — with Glasgow Southside MSP championing the cause.

stories.summary: Government pages confirm the Burnham cabinet structure with Andy Burnham as PM and updated ministerial appointments across departments including the Home Office and FCDO.

stories.summary: A consultancy has been engaged to support the new Future Civil Service initiative, pointing to continued use of external private sector expertise in Whitehall reform efforts.

stories.summary: Politico reports that Westminster constituency has been identified as a Lib Dem target seat, marking a significant shift in electoral geography.
